thread:
Alex R: FYI we just got a page from the client-facing cluster, high throttles reported. hitting 5xxs for a handful of VIP tenants. paging oncall now.
SRE Bot: :rotating_light: Pager: INC-2026-445 created. Severity: P2. Channels: #eng-sre, #incidents. Oncall: Jin L. Paging Jin L.
Jin L (oncall): I'm on it. quick summary? which region?
Alex R: eu-west-1. Symptoms: elevated `throttle_count` and user-facing 502s. Queue depth spiked on the text-gen pool. tokens/sec dropped due to backpressure.
Devin S: I'm looking at metrics. queue_depth per-pod jumped from 120 -> ~1400 around 03:12 UTC. throttles/sec spiked to ~40 for the service. 95th latency for gpt-lite also climbed.
Sam P: Logs show a batcher stall in runtime-2, repeated kernel OOMs causing retries. I can attach the stack traces in a sec.
Taylor L: Any customer impact list? need to inform CS.
Alex R: CS asked: 3 customers saw errors in last 30m; two are paying enterprise. Flagged to account team.
SRE Bot: Incident timeline note: INC-2026-445 created at 1862345678. Auto-runbook step: run `redwood ops status autoscale`.
Jin L (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) scale dedicated pool by +25% (burst), 2) reduce max_batch_size for the runtime config, 3) temporarily mute noisy queue_depth alert while we tune. Who can run the scale?
Devin S: I'll trigger a scale up. running: `redwoodctl scale pool text-gen-eu --instances +3`. Confirming resource availability.
Sam P: While scaling, do we want to adjust alert thresholds? queue_depth threshold is currently 500. Given recent workload patterns that's too aggressive — false positives during bursts.
Alex R: Agreed. Proposal: change queue_depth alert from >500 for 5m to >1200 for 5m, and add a tokens_per_sec alert: tokens/sec < 20000 for 3m AND throttle_rate > 10 => page.
Taylor L: Also propose adding a dashboard card: tokens/sec per-customer top5, and throttle events heatmap across runtimes. That will help ops triage.
Jin L (oncall): Scale up done (confirmed). Pool CPU/GPU usage still high but not saturating. Throttles dropping from 40 -> 6 in the last 4m.
Devin S: Reduced max_batch_size in runtime config from 64 -> 40: editing config and restarting batcher on two pods. Patch applied.
SRE Bot: Deploy bot: config-change applied to runtime-2 (rev 2026.03.12-rt2). No failures. Rolling restart started.
Sam P: Patch logs: I saw a kernel mem spike but no OOMs after restart. Batcher latencies normalized.
Alex R: CS update: told the two enterprises that we saw transient throttling, mitigations applied, monitoring in place. They asked for RCA and ETA for permanent fix.
Devin S: For RCA: combination of unexpected request fanout from a customer test + our aggressive queue_depth alert threshold. Also a code path in sampler increased batch memory briefly.
Taylor L: Action items (from incident):
- T1: Update Prometheus alert rule (queue_depth) and add tokens/sec + throttle correlation rule. Owner: Sam P. ETA: today EOD.
- T2: New Ops dashboard with tokens/sec per-customer, throttle heatmap, per-runtime queue percentiles. Owner: Devin S. ETA: 48h.
- T3: Runbook update: add step to check tokens/sec and prefer scaling before muting alerts. Owner: Jin L. ETA: 24h.
- T4: Follow-up eval on model sampling changes that increased memory. Owner: Alex R + ML runtime team. ETA: 1 week.
Sam P: Draft alert rule snippet I'm going to push:
```
- alert: HighQueueDepthAdjusted
  expr: sum(queue_depth{service="text-gen",region="eu-west-1"}) by (pool) > 1200
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/queue-depth

- alert: TokensAndThrottleCorrelation
  expr: (rate(tokens_processed[3m]) < 20000) and (increase(throttle_count[3m]) > 10)
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
```
Sam P: I'll also add a `snooze` rule to silence old queue_depth alerts during active scaling windows: tag `autoscale:in-progress`.
Devin S: For dashboards I'll add a topN query for tokens/sec by tenant:
```
topk(5, sum(rate(tokens_processed[1m])) by (tenant))
```
Jin L (oncall): I'm going to mute the existing high-noise rule for 30m while we confirm new thresholds. Doing: `alerts silence set --id queue-depth --duration 30m --reason "tuning during incident"`.
SRE Bot: Silence created: silence-789 (expires in 30m).
Alex R: Customer comms: request a post-incident summary with timeline + what we changed. Can we have a short blameless RCA for them?
Taylor L: I'll draft the summary once owners update the task list. Keep it factual: what happened, impact, mitigation, and next steps.
Devin S: Observability note: add 99th latency and p50/p95 bins to the same dashboard to see latency vs queue depth correlation.
Sam P: Pushed alert rule to staging. Running a canary of the new rule with 24h evaluation: `alerts deploy --env staging --rule-file alerts/queue-depth-adjusted.yml`.
Jin L (oncall): I'll hand off to second oncall in 30m. if throttles return we re-escalate.
Alex R: Thanks all. Marking INC-2026-445 as mitigated for now. Keep the runbook and alerts tickets open until we finish postmortem tasks.
SRE Bot: Incident INC-2026-445 status: mitigated. Duration: ~22m. Follow-ups: queue-depth-tuning (task-452), dashboard-work (task-453), runtime-rca (task-454).
Taylor L: Filing postmortem doc stub: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-445 (will add timeline and owners). Please add any notes.
Devin S: Quick note for follow-up: consider switching primary autoscale signal from queue_depth to tokens/sec-derived metric for text-gen pools. queue_depth is sensitive to bursty batch sizes.
Sam P: Agree. tokens/sec is more stable across model variants. Will prototype a tokens-based autoscale metric next sprint.
Jin L (oncall): Handoff: I'm leaving the incident in monitoring. Next oncall: @Taylor L at 1862345900.
Taylor L: taking over. thanks team. :thumbsup:
